current.text: He is Atlanta's clear starting center, with little competition for his role. Veesaar is out for the season, Gueye is injured, and Jock Landale is the main backup.
Atlanta is reported to be very cautious with his minutes.
Quin Snyder wants him spaced away from the rim when he plays with Dyson Daniels and Jalen Johnson.
Experts do not expect his FG% or his block rate to bounce back under Quin Snyder, because his role away from the rim and the defensive scheme stay the same.
His usage was 19.5 with Trae Young out and fell to 17 and then 16 late last season. His usage and scoring dropped when he shared the floor with CJ McCollum.
The idea that Porzingis leaving boosts his role is overstated.

Experts call his rank of 49 a little too high for category leagues. They say nine-cat rankings inflate him, a round 4 pick would disappoint, and a pick in the 50s or 60s is fair, mostly as a positional pick at center.
In an auction mock, Josh targeted him at 15 to 16 USD and bought him for 16 USD.
Atlanta plays 4, 4 and 3 games in our playoff weeks 19 to 21. The team has 14 back-to-backs and is not expected to rest or shut down players.

durable.text: He is a stretch center who takes many threes. He shot 38% from three on real volume, and the volume should hold even if the percentage dips.
For a center, his threes and steals are clearly above average. His blocks and rebounds are only average for the position.
Since moving to the perimeter, his rim finishing and offensive rebound rate are lower, and his assist rate and three-point rate are higher.
He gave up blocks to cut fouls and defend on the perimeter, so his block rate is lower and his steal rate is higher. Expect this profile to continue, maybe with a few more blocks.
He has very good hands and feel, and he handles the ball better than most centers.
He is not a big rebounder, but he is a usable second center.
His broad profile of threes, steals and blocks makes him worth more in category leagues than in points leagues.
Quin Snyder runs a high-movement, five-out offense that wants many threes.

note: He went for 6 USD in our league last season. Yahoo values him at 22 USD and ESPN at 14 USD, but average costs are only 7.7 and 6.3 USD, and an expert auction mock paid 16 USD. For a center he helps every build with threes and steals and has no weak category, but experts expect his FG% (48%, down from 57%) and his blocks to stay at last season's lower level. Treat him as a mid-priced second center, not a round 4 value. Early in the season, check his minutes, his usage next to McCollum, and whether Snyder gives him more shots at the rim.
